analysis.title: GS Crypto: Unwind
key_insights: BTC and ETH touched weekend lows of about $62k and $1,711, then stabilized near $65k and $1,826 in Monday's Asia session. BTC is down 16% month to date and 26% year to date.
Both assets have fully unwound the price inflection that began on 19 August. BTC is back at pre-19 August levels and ETH is slightly below its August range.
Gold moved higher in August and inflected sharply on 19 August, and BTC and ETH followed. Gold was already below its 19 August range by mid-September, and BTC has now caught up with that adjustment.
The desk says the conditions and catalysts behind the August rally have reversed, and in some cases worsened. It lists macro, regulation, ETF flows and technicals as the four drivers.

Macro: last week's CPI print surprised meaningfully to the upside, the third consecutive month of less favorable inflation data. Markets price three hikes into early Q2 next year. The Fed's hawkish shift is likely to keep debasement concerns contained, which removes the narrative that supported gold and BTC in August.

Yields and the dollar are higher than in August: the 10-year is at 5.14% versus 4.70%, the 30-year at 5.47% versus 5.28%, and DXY at the 103 handle versus the 98 handle. A stronger dollar and higher yields pressure non-yielding assets.

Regulation: the CLARITY Act failed to advance, and the August catalyst of the White House crypto event, where the President urged lawmakers to pass it, did not turn into legislation. Some view the midterms blue-wave outcome as a more challenging legislative backdrop for crypto. Agency-channel regulatory developments have continued.
ETF flows: US spot BTC ETFs lost $1bn last week, taking year-to-date net flows to -$1.9bn. US spot ETH ETFs had $398m of net outflows last week, taking year-to-date net flows to -$804m.

Technicals: BTC lost its 200-day moving average on 12 November, then fell below its 200-week moving average (around $68k) on 14 November. Thin weekend liquidity made the breakdown trigger forced selling, with $1.78bn of BTC liquidations across 13-15 November.
Perpetual futures funding has fallen back to flat as of Monday, which reflects reduced net long positioning.

Options: downside protection is better bid than upside, with BTC 1-month 25-delta risk reversals at -5.09%. The desk says those wanting to fade the move might fund calls by selling puts, given current positioning.
